summary:
### EarthScope: Understanding How Our Planet Is Changing

EarthScope is a project created to explore how our planet is changing and what these changes mean for the future. Using NASA's Earth observation data, we aim to identify environmental trends such as rising temperatures, changing rainfall patterns, loss of vegetation, melting ice, and other signs of climate change.

Our idea is to make scientific information easier for everyone to understand, not just scientists. We want to turn complex satellite data into simple visualizations and comparisons that allow people to see how different parts of the world are changing over time.

As students, we believe that understanding environmental problems is the first step toward addressing them. This project gives people an opportunity to look beyond statistics and recognize the real changes happening around them. We hope EarthScope can encourage curiosity, raise environmental awareness, and help communities make more informed decisions about protecting our planet.
details:
Project Details – EarthScope: Be an Earth Trend Detective

EarthScope is a student-led project inspired by the idea that understanding our planet should be easier and more accessible to everyone. The project aims to use NASA's Earth observation data to explore environmental changes, including rising temperatures, changing rainfall patterns, vegetation loss, and changes in ice and water systems.

The way EarthScope is designed to work is simple. Users can explore different environmental indicators, select geographical regions, and compare observations over time. The information is then presented through graphs, visual comparisons, and simple explanations that help users recognize patterns and understand what they mean.

One of the main benefits of this project is that it makes scientific information less complicated. Instead of looking at large amounts of data and unfamiliar statistics, users can explore environmental changes in a more visual and understandable way. We hope this encourages students, researchers, and communities to become more curious about environmental issues.

What makes EarthScope creative is its focus on turning people into active Earth Trend Detectives. Rather than simply presenting facts about climate change, it encourages users to investigate, compare, ask questions, and discover patterns for themselves.

For the project concept and demonstration, we used Microsoft PowerPoint to design the presentation and create an illustrative dashboard. Our planned development would involve NASA's publicly available Earth observation datasets, data visualization tools, and programming technologies such as Python, JavaScript, and HTML/CSS.

Throughout the design process, we considered accessibility, simplicity, scientific accuracy, geographical differences, and the importance of presenting information responsibly. We also considered that environmental changes can affect different communities in different ways.

Our intended impact is to make people more aware of the changes happening on our planet and encourage them to use scientific information to understand and care for the environment. As students, we believe that meaningful change begins with curiosity, knowledge, and the willingness to ask questions.
